learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected pH 1.0 for acetic acid at the same 0.10 mol/L as hydrochloric acid and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Pressed Dissolve HCl, then Dissolve CH3COOH. Both buttons became disabled after use; reveal unlocked only after both. Screenshot showed hydrochloric 75 of 75 split, pH 1.0; acetic 1 of 75 split, pH 2.9.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 2.9. Explains fewer free H+ means higher pH, strength is share giving up H+ rather than amount in bottle; strong hydrochloric versus weak acetic.
observations.visual: Inline screenshot inspected: left beaker has many separate red hydrogen dots and outlined partners, right mostly paired white molecules with one red dot. Counts and pH labels above beakers legible. Trust count 5/5 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884122 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Equal concentration setup clearly tests strength-versus-amount misconception.

interaction.reason: Two dissolve actions reveal relevant contrast but fixed one-shot state limits experimentation.
interaction.evidence: Each button disabled after use; 75 versus 1 split.

payoff.reason: Directly ties counts to pH and distinction between strength and amount.

clarity.reason: Beaker counts, molecular dots and pH legend make intended comparison legible.
clarity.evidence: Inspected screenshot and successful two-button path.

transfer.reason: Reusable strength/concentration distinction given without concrete new application or conditions.
transfer.evidence: Strength is share giving up H+ rather than amount.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Equal-pH prediction overturned by contrasting free-ion counts.

visualExplanation.reason: Molecular pairing and red free-ion dots carry mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Fixed one-shot dissolve actions offer little reversible discovery.
playfulness.evidence: Both buttons disabled at end; no reset visible.

practicalValue.reason: Bottle concentration versus strength distinction is concrete chemistry interpretation.
practicalValue.evidence: Vinegar acid and hydrochloric acid comparison.

depth.reason: Links molecular dissociation, ion count and logarithmic pH.

complexity.reason: Links split molecular share to free ions and pH with counted visual support.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Several linked representations but one central comparison.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: chemical formulas, H+, mol/L, logarithmic relation

whyCool: Dissolving equal amounts makes one beaker release 75 hydrogen dots and the other only one, turning an invisible chemical difference into a count.
caveat: Fixed illustrative sample offers no concentration variation, equilibrium dynamics or repeat/reset path.
